families.label: Raw / Scavenged
families.role: What the world gives. Nothing here is crafted; everything else is made from it.
rules: Seven backbone raws carry the language: Wood (frames, handles, fuel), Stone (mass, heads, hearths), Fiber (binding, cloth), Hide (leather, padding), Iron Ore (all metal), Parts (anything mechanical), Crystal (anything Core).
A scavenged raw is a made thing the player cannot make: Parts, Electronic Parts, Resistor Wire, Tin Can, Needle Tube. Each gates one technology and has no formula on purpose.
A creature raw names its use: Hide and Fur are worn, Fat is burned or injected, Shell is lime, Gland is medicine, Chitin is plate, Feather is fletching.
No raw has a crafting formula. Crude Petroleum is the one raw with a job row (`pump_crude`): that row is extraction from finite seep stock, not a craft.
examples: Parts: in 23 bills, never craftable, also the research currency. The scarce hand on every machine.
Tin Can: the container of every preserved food. No tin, no soup, wine, jam or canned meat.
Resistor Wire: one consumer (the Powered Door lock). A deliberate single-purpose electrical scrap.
families.infer: Seeing "Parts" in a bill tells the player the product has moving or fitted pieces; seeing "Electronic Parts" tells them it will need power.

families.label: Processed Materials / Components
families.role: One processing step away from raw, or a purpose-built part. These are the words recipes are written in.
rules: First-step materials cost exactly one raw and one station: Charcoal (wood, fire), Iron Ingot (ore, furnace), Leather (hide, bench), Rope and Cloth (fiber), Plank (wood).
Refined Iron is iron plus carbon: 3 Iron + 2 Charcoal -> 2. It is the marker of tier 2 metal.
Four components each mean one thing wherever they appear: Gear = a mechanism that turns; Pipe = a tube or a hollow structural member; Plate = sheet metal that protects; Blade = a cutting edge.
A component is metal + Parts at a level-2 bench. Plain iron for Gear and Blade, Refined Iron for Pipe and Plate. Pipe and Plate share one bill and both yield 2.
Needle and Thread means "this is sewn". It appears in every stitched armour piece and in travel gear, nowhere else.
examples: Gear 2 Iron + 3 Parts: the Parts-heaviest component, as in Last Island (50 iron + 65 parts).
Blade 3 Iron + 1 Part: cheaper than a Gear, as in Last Island (30 + 15).
Pipe / Plate 2 Refined Iron + 2 Parts -> 2: same bill, different shape.
families.infer: Knowing Pipe and Plate, a player who meets the Utility Frame (Pipe + Iron + Refined Iron + Parts) reads it as "a tube skeleton with fittings" without being told.

families.label: Food / Medicine / Consumables
families.role: Things used up by using them: eaten, drunk, applied or burned.
rules: Fire turns one raw food into one better food, 1:1: Meat -> Roast or Dried, Marsh Cap -> Grilled.
A Tin Can turns several raw foods into one dense, slot-efficient food: soup, canned meat, wine, jam. The tin is the cost of density.
Each cooked food buys a different thing: Roast = hunger, Dried = weight, Canned = slots, Soup = warmth, Juice = thirst, Wine = portable warmth, Jam = stamina, Stew = the best meal and needs a farm.
Medicine climbs in three steps: Bandage (fiber), Medkit (bandages + herb), Syringe (a scavenged Needle Tube + fat + iron). Purge Tonic treats radiation and needs a Mire Gland.
A water container is made once and refilled; fuel is made per can.
examples: Roast Meat 1 Meat, 8 s vs Dried Meat 1 Meat, 20 s: less hunger, half the weight.
Mushroom Soup 5 Marsh Cap + 1 Tin: Last Island numbers, literal.
Fuel Canister: 3 Crude + 1 Glass, or 5 Crude + 1 Glass for two, or 6 Fat + 1 Cloth without any oil.
families.infer: A player who has made Mushroom Soup (5 + tin) and Fruit Wine (5 berries + tin) expects any new tinned food to be "about five of something plus a tin".

families.label: Tools / Non-Core Weapons
families.role: Held items that wear with use. Cores are the main weapon system; these are tools and side arms.
rules: Three tool tiers, same shape each time: Stone (wood + stone + rope, by hand), Iron (3 Iron + 2 wood + 1 leather, bench 1), Salvager (the Iron tool itself + 2 Refined Iron + a Pipe, bench 2).
An axe and a pick of one tier cost the same, except where the head differs: the Stone Pick takes one more stone, the Salvager Axe takes a Blade.
Every edged weapon above stone is priced in Blades: Cleaver 1, Reinforced Spear 1, Machete 3.
An upgrade consumes the thing it upgrades (Salvager tools consume the Iron tool), so progress is never two parallel grinds.
Weapons with no metal are made by hand and are disposable: Club, Fire-hardened Spear, Torch.
examples: Stone Axe 3 wood + 3 stone + 1 rope -> Iron Axe 3 Iron + 2 wood + 1 leather -> Salvager Axe = Iron Axe + Blade + 2 Refined Iron + Pipe.
Cleaver 1 Iron + 1 Blade; Machete 4 Iron + 3 Blades.
Arrow 6 per wood + stone + fiber; 8 per wood + stone + feather.
families.infer: Knowing the Iron Axe and the Salvager Axe, the Salvager Pick is predictable: the Iron Pick plus the same Refined Iron and Pipe, without the Blade.

families.label: Armour / Clothing / Carry
families.role: Worn items. Five slots: head, body, back, legs, feet.
rules: Soft gear is hide or fur tied with rope: Leather Jerkin, Fur Cloak.
An Iron Plate piece is Plate + 3 Hide + 3 Needle and Thread. Only the plate count changes with the area covered: boots 1, helmet 1, pants 2, chest 3 (chest also takes 4 hide).
A Refined Iron piece is Refined Iron + 5 Hide + 6 Needle and Thread: helmet, legs and boots 3 ingots; chest 5 ingots and 8 thread.
Hide is always the padding and Needle and Thread always the assembly. Metal is the only term that changes between the two sets.
Special protection names its special material: Filter Mask = glass lens + cloth filter + Parts; Chitin Plate = chitin + leather.
examples: Iron Plate Boots 1 Plate + 3 Hide + 3 Thread; Iron Plate Chest 3 Plate + 4 Hide + 3 Thread.
Refined Iron Helmet 3 Refined + 5 Hide + 6 Thread; Refined Iron Chest 5 Refined + 5 Hide + 8 Thread.
Trail Pack 2 Cloth + 2 Leather + 2 Thread + 2 Rope: sewn, so it carries Thread.
families.infer: A player with Iron Plate Helmet and Chest can guess the Pants (between them: 2 Plate) and the Boots (same as the helmet: 1 Plate).

families.label: Cores / Energies
families.role: The SOH weapon system that replaces Last Island firearms. A Core is the weapon; Energy and Essence are its ammunition.
rules: Every Core is Iron (housing) + Parts (mechanism) + Crystal (focus). That triple is the Core signature and appears nowhere else as a set.

Common Cores are the bare triple (2 Iron, 4 Parts, 1 Crystal). Rare Cores scale the triple and add the raw of their element: Sulfur for fire, Shell for water, Electronic Parts for lightning, Crawler Optic for spirit. The top Core doubles a rare one.
Energy is ammunition by tier: Basic from stone and fiber by hand; Refined from Crystal and Iron at a level-2 bench; a level-3 bench makes it in bulk with Charcoal.
An Essence is the element raw plus one binder, two per craft: Sulfur + Charcoal (fire), Bitterleaf + its seed (nature), Shell + Crystal (water), Crawler Optic + Crystal (spirit).
The four charge Cores (Ember, Quake, Storm, Rime) are an older single-element design: element raw + 8 to 10 Parts + Crystal, known only through study.
examples: Big Bang 2 Iron + 4 Parts + 1 Crystal -> Meteor 4 Iron + 8 Parts + 3 Crystal + 3 Sulfur -> Dragon's Breath 8 + 16 + 6 + 6.
Elsa's Sword 3 Iron + 8 Parts + 4 Crystal + 3 Shell: water, so Shell.
Refined Energy 1 Crystal + 1 Iron -> 4; bulk 2 + 2 + 2 Charcoal -> 12.
families.infer: Knowing Meteor (fire, Sulfur) and Elsa's Sword (water, Shell), a player who finds a lightning Core expects the triple plus an electrical raw, and Mjolnir is exactly that.

families.label: Home / Storage / Workstations
families.role: Packed devices carried in the pack and placed in the world, where they become a structure with hit points.
rules: A pack is paid for once, by hand, and placing it costs nothing more. Picking the structure up returns the same pack.
A pack costs what the thing is made of: wood and stone for the hearth tier (Campfire, Furnace, Workbench, Chest), iron when it holds weight, Parts when it has a mechanism.
A machine that moves fluid has Pipe; one that turns has a Gear; one that sees or decides has Electronic Parts.
A bigger version of a station repeats the smaller one's material and adds the next tier's: the Large Furnace doubles the Furnace stone and adds iron, Plate and a charcoal bed.
examples: Furnace 18 stone + 4 wood -> Large Furnace 36 stone + 8 Iron + 4 Plate + 4 Charcoal.
Oil Pump 3 Iron + 1 Gear + 2 Pipe + 2 Parts; Oil Refinery 8 Iron + 8 wood + 2 Pipe + 5 Parts + 2 Glass.
Wood Chest 8 wood -> Iron-bound Chest 12 wood + 2 Iron.
families.infer: Knowing the Oil Pump has a Gear (it pumps) and Pipe (it carries), the Refinery is readable: Pipe again, Glass for the still, no Gear because nothing turns.

families.label: Electricity / Defense
rules: Anything that carries or switches current has Iron + Electronic Parts + Parts. A cable is the bare conductor: Iron + Fiber.
A sensor differs from a switch only in what triggers it: the Pressure Switch adds a Plate to stand on.
A mechanical trap has a Gear and no electronics: Bear Trap, Arrow Turret.
A wooden obstacle is wood only: Spikes, Barricade.
The Powered Door is a module fitted to a door already built, so it has a build cost and no pack.
examples: Power Switch 1 Iron + 2 Electronic Parts + 1 Parts; Infrared Sensor the same; Pressure Switch adds 1 Iron + 1 Plate.
Bear Trap 1 Gear + 2 Iron; Arrow Turret 10 wood + 2 Iron + 1 Gear + 2 rope.
Powered Door module 2 Iron + 2 Electronic Parts + 1 Gear + 2 Plate + 2 Resistor Wire.
families.infer: Knowing the Power Switch and the Bear Trap, the Powered Door is the sum: electronics to decide, a Gear to move the bolt, Plate for the leaf.

families.label: Mobility / Traversal
families.role: Getting further, carrying more, crossing what blocks a walk.
rules: A vehicle is a frame plus what moves it. The Hand Cart is wood, iron and rope. The Motorbike is a Utility Frame + Gears + Plates + Refined Iron at a level-3 bench.
A ladder is wood and rope. The steel one consumes the wooden one and adds Refined Iron and a Gear for the fold.
examples: Wooden Ladder 12 wood + 1 rope -> Steel Folding Ladder = Wooden Ladder + 6 Refined Iron + 1 Gear.
Hand Cart 24 wood + 3 Iron + 4 rope.
Motorbike = Frame + 2 Gears + 3 Plates + 4 Refined Iron.
families.infer: The Steel Ladder follows the Salvager-tool rule from family 04: the better item contains the lesser one plus refined metal and one component.

families.label: Farming / Husbandry
rules: A seed is never crafted: it comes from the plant.
Fodder is fiber plus a seed: bulk plus feed value.
examples: Fodder Bundle 3 fiber + 1 Wild Berry Seed -> 3.
families.infer: A seed in a bill (Fodder, Nature Essence) always competes with planting it.

families.label: Knowledge / Access / Unique
families.role: Items whose value is what they unlock or prove. None is crafted.
rules: A Blueprint is a recipe on paper. It is produced by research, not by a bench.
A specimen teaches one formula when studied and is consumed by the study.
An access card is a physical key with a finite number of scans. Crafting one would defeat the lock.
Elder stones, boss relics and Ragnarok Cash are earned once from a specific fight or from the run economy.
examples: Boar Tusk -> study -> Machete formula.
Beetle Horn -> study -> Chitin Plate formula.
families.infer: If it proves something or opens something, it has no formula.

alternatives.trade: Three routes. Fat route: no oil chain, but 6 fat per can and the slowest. Refinery single against batch: batch is cheaper and faster per can, and gives up only batch size (5 Crude and room for 2 cans). The single route is therefore weak. It belongs to the oil workstream (#59) and was left as is.
Bulk route needs a level-3 bench and Charcoal; per unit it saves a third of the Crystal and Iron.
Refined route (2 Refined Iron + Pipe, study) against Parts route (Gear + 2 Parts = 5 Parts, starter-known). Furnace time against scarce Parts.
Fiber gives 6, a Feather gives 8. Feathers come only from grouse.
Rich Ore route: 1 ore instead of 3 ingots and faster, but Rich Ore needs an iron-class pick and is a separate, scarcer world material.
Crystal route (inland, study, competes with Cores) against Shell route (coast, starter-known, slower, two of each).
